extracted.intended_audience: readers, librarians, and researchers looking for information about short story anthologies
extracted.subtask_description: Describes the editorial selection process and scope for The Best American Short Stories series (1995 volume): how works are chosen for inclusion and the geographic/source limits. Useful for understanding anthology curation rather than providing writing advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Series editorial selection process
rubrics_metrics.description: Each volume's series editor selects notable works from hundreds of periodicals. A special guest editor then chooses the best twenty or so pieces to publish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-stage selection: series editor compiles a long list of notable works; guest editor makes the final selection of roughly twenty pieces for publication. This is presented as the defining method that lends the series its reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source and geographic scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Selected from U.S. and Canadian magazines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility/scope is limited to works appearing in periodicals published in the United States and Canada (i.e., the anthology draws from North American magazines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notability / quality implied by selection
rubrics_metrics.description: The series is described as the premier annual showcase for the country's finest short fiction and nonfiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied evaluative standard: works chosen are among the 'finest' and 'notable' from the pool of periodical publications, although the page does not spell out explicit literary criteria (e.g., craft, theme, innovation).
